transcript:
MEETING HEADER
Date: 2026-06-02
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Jamie (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Priya (Head of Data, Aurum), Marcus (CTO), Anna (POC Manager)

SUMMARY:
Quick scoping POC focused on extracting structured financial fields and intent from PDFs and email threads across en/fr/es. Discussed model shortlist (open models), quality vs cost tradeoffs, benchmark metrics (precision/recall on named fields, latency p95, tokens/sec), infra sizing for pilot, and compliance needs (SOC 2, KMS, VPC). Next steps: share benchmark spreadsheet, test harness design, customer to provide sample data.

TOPICS COVERED:
- POC scope and success criteria
- Workload sizing and expected qps/burst patterns
- Candidate open-model shortlist and quantization tradeoffs
- Multilingual requirements and domain adaptation
- Security/compliance (data residency, KMS, audit logs)
- Timeline and pilot kickoff

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Alex (AE): hey everyone, uh thanks for joining. quick intros — i'm alex from redwood, jamie and ravi here on the se side.
[00:09] Priya: thanks, priya here, head of data at aurum. we run the ops on the loan ops and KYC pipelines. excited to scope this.
[00:16] Marcus: marcus, cto. i'll be pretty involved on infra and security side.
[00:21] Alex: great, goal for today is to nail down success criteria and shortlist models for the POC, and figure out what benchmark we run.
[00:29] Jamie (SE): quick framing — you told us offline you're seeing PDFs, emails, and scanned statements, right? mix of structured and unstructured, some OCR errors in the scans?
[00:40] Priya: yes exactly. PDFs with native text about 70%, scanned images about 30% with variable OCR quality. languages are english primarily, then french and spanish ~10% combined.
[00:52] Ravi (SE): good to know. for the POC we'd recommend we focus on canonical fields first — account number, ledger balance, transaction dates, payee names, and sanction-check flags. that gives a measurable set for precision/recall.
[01:05] Anna (POC Manager): can we also track intent classification for emails — e.g. payment request vs statement inquiry — because we route those?
[01:12] Jamie: yes that's in scope, intent classifier is a smaller task but important for routing.
[01:17] Marcus: timeline wise — we want a two-week bench run and then a pilot for 4 weeks. target go/no-go in ~6 weeks total. is that realistic?
[01:26] Alex: that's reasonable for a POC, depends on how fast we can get data and infra.
[01:30] 
[05:02] Alex: on success criteria — what metric triggers acceptance? priya?
[05:07] Priya: key thing is field extraction accuracy. we want >92% F1 on the canonical fields on native text and >85% on scanned docs. Latency target p95 under 800ms for single-document extraction for hosted mode. throughput for pilot estimate is ~50 qps sustained with spikes to 200 qps for batch loads. cost target — we want to keep inference cost under $0.01 per document on average.
[05:36] Jamie: okay so accuracy, p95 latency, throughput, and cost. we'll capture those in the bench spreadsheet.
[05:45] 
[07:10] Ravi: talking model shortlist — since you asked open models, we propose: Mistral Large, Falcon-180B-instruct (quantized), Llama3-13B variants, and an adapted open-llama-ish 34B where we apply LoRA and domain fine-tune. also consider local hybrid approach: small encoder for extraction + seq2seq for normalization.
[07:34] Priya: are those good for multilingual? french/spanish?
[07:37] Jamie: some models handle multilingual better — Llama3 family has good multi-ling support, Mistral is ok, Falcon often weaker on non-en unless tuned. we should shortlist 2-3 to test across languages.
[07:49] Marcus: curious about quantization tradeoffs — we need to run 4-bit/8-bit tests; how much quality do we lose?
[07:55] Jamie: in our experience, 8-bit usually preserves quality for extraction tasks, 4-bit can be hit-or-miss: sometimes slight drop in NER performance, especially on rare tokens like client IDs. but 4-bit gives cost/throughput wins. we'll quantify on the bench run.
[08:12] Anna: for privacy we prefer private deployment, but for speed initial POC could be hosted with strict retention. what do you recommend?
[08:19] Alex: common path is hosted for speed, using VPC peering and short retention, then switch to dedicated or private if you need keys in KMS or stricter residency. we'll map both options in the pilot plan.
[08:29] 
[12:01] Priya: sample volumes — monthly ingestion is ~1.5M documents, peak day ~150k, average doc size 1-2 pages. for pilot we can give 10k representative docs.
[12:13] Jamie: that's helpful. for sizing we'll propose GPU types and pooling strategy; e.g., A100/RTX 6000 style for latency, plus batched worker pools for throughput.
[12:24] Ravi: also want to measure cold-start vs KV-cache benefits; many of your docs share prefixes (bank headers) so prefix caching might help.
[12:33] Marcus: on compliance — we need SOC2 plus KMS integration and ability to audit token-level logs without exposing raw PII. can you support that?
[12:43] Alex: yes we have KMS integrations and can provide audit logging + redaction hooks. we'll send security docs.
[12:48] 
[18:00] Jamie: bench metrics we'll measure: field-level precision/recall, overall extraction F1, intent classifier accuracy, p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per doc, memory footprint per model, and failure/error rates. we should also include a small adversarial set (noisy OCR) and per-language breakdown.
[18:20] Priya: good, also want human-in-the-loop fallback rate — when to route to ops for manual review.
[18:27] Jamie: yes we'll add that as an operational metric.
[18:32] 
[22:10] Alex: on model priortization for the POC: we suggest run three candidates — a smaller Llama3-ish 13B quantized (good latency), a Mistral 30- or 40B-ish variant for quality, and a tuned Falcon-like 34B with LoRA for finance domain. we'll test 8-bit as baseline and 4-bit for cost ops.
[22:34] Marcus: what about an ensemble approach — small model for extraction, big model for edge cases?
[22:38] Jamie: that's feasible; ensemble reduces avg cost and only hotspots hit the larger model. we'll include ensemble in bench plan as a variant.
[22:46] 
[26:00] Anna: sample data sharing — we can redact PII and drop raw ids. prefer S3 upload to a presigned bucket.
[26:08] Alex: perfect, we'll share a minimal manifest and expected schema for upload.
[26:12] Priya: any constraints around residency? all data stored and processed in eu-west-1 preferred.
[26:17] Alex: we can route pilot workloads to eu-west region; dedicated/private options can be on-prem later.
[26:22] 
[30:50] Ravi: about evaluation harness — we'll provide a python test harness that runs model endpoints, computes metrics, and aggregates cost. It will support hosted API or your private endpoint with a small adapter.
[30:59] Priya: that sounds good, we want reproducible bench runs and a shared google sheet for the results.
[31:05] Alex: we'll push results to the sheet and include breakdown per model, per language, per document type.
[31:12] 
[35:00] Marcus: questions on security — how are keys stored?
[35:04] Alex: in hosted we can integrate with your KMS via customer-managed keys in the dedicated/private path; for hosted short-retention we still support envelope encryption and audit logs.
[35:12] Marcus: ok please include SOC 2 and encryption details in the docs.
[35:16] 
[38:40] Jamie: risks — OCR noise, edge-case entity formats, and multilingual rare tokens. mitigation: pre-OCR cleanup, small human labeling batch for re-tuning, and LoRA on small curated dataset.
[38:52] Priya: budget question — what's a rough cost estimate for the pilot run?
[38:56] Alex: rough ballpark: using hosted instances and 3 models for 2 weeks of bench plus pilot, expect $6-10k depending on model sizes and quantization choices. we'll give a more precise number after we size with your sample data.
[39:12] 
[40:00] Anna: ok next steps recap?
[40:03] Alex: i'll send benchmark spreadsheet, model shortlist, and security summary by friday 2026-06-04.
[40:08] Jamie: i'll draft test harness and infra sizing by monday 2026-06-05.
[40:12] Anna: we'll upload sample data and the success criteria doc by 2026-06-08.
[40:18] Marcus: schedule kickoff week of 15th, tentatively 2026-06-16.
[40:22] Alex: perfect. any final q's?
[40:25] Priya: none here, thanks all.
[40:28] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links.

ACTION ITEMS (RECAPPED IN TRANSCRIPT):
